column3: The Hebrew explicitly names the LORD twice; BSB uses “He” for the second occurrence.
The Hebrew says the wife had not given birth and uses a singular collective designation for the Danite; BSB says she “had no children” and uses plural “Danites.”
The Hebrew says she has not given birth; BSB says she has “no children.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has both “said” and “saying” and repeats the appearance noun; BSB gives “told” and names “appearance” once.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew asks what they should “do for” the child; BSB specifies “how to raise” him.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew separately says she hurried, ran, told, and said; BSB combines the reporting into running quickly to tell her husband.
The Hebrew says “the woman”; BSB specifies “my wife.”
The Hebrew opens with “Now let your words come”; BSB makes this “When your words come to pass.”
The Hebrew says the woman must guard against everything spoken to her; BSB recasts this as doing everything she was told.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “let us detain you” and prepare the goat “before you”; BSB has “Please stay here” and “for you.”
The Hebrew says “if you detain me” and names “your bread”; BSB has “Even if I stay” and “your food.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the subject of doing wonderfully unnamed; BSB explicitly names “the LORD” again.
The Hebrew repeats “the altar” with the second flame reference; BSB says simply “the flame.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names Manoah and repeats the dying verb for emphasis; BSB uses “he” and “We are going to die.”
The Hebrew has singular “our hand” and says God caused them to hear this “at this time”; BSB has plural “our hands” and says “spoken to us this way.”
Close to the Hebrew.
